- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.40) in recent days, model tends to overcorrect upward — reduce forecast peak by 5–10%.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 70), model often overshoots and fails to correct — cap forecast at +5% above peak or adjust downward if sentiment turns neutral or negative.
- If sentiment is consistently positive (e.g., > 0.20) over 3–5 days, model tends to overestimate — apply a 3–7% downward bias to avoid overconfidence.
- Model often underestimates true price volatility in the final 5–7 days of forecast horizon — add 2–5% upward adjustment if sentiment is neutral or slightly positive.
- If sentiment shows strong reversal (e.g., from -0.5 to +0.3 within 3 days), model lags — adjust forecast to reflect sentiment shift 1–2 days ahead.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is > 75% above 30-day moving average, reduce by 10–15% unless sentiment supports continuation.
- For 30-day forecasts, avoid assuming linear continuation — if sentiment is volatile, use 2–3 day smoothing or exponential decay weighting.
